learning: If the score returns to about 69 with line loss at or below 1 per run, kd has little effect and the next lever is line-loss handling. If the score rises, keep kd 0.4 and test a further small increase. If the score falls or oscillation rises above about 0.15, return kd to 0.3.
notes: Reference geometry with the iteration 1 controller restored (base_speed 1.3), and kd raised from 0.3 to 0.4 as the only change. base_speed 1.15 was rejected by iteration 7 (61.77).
rationale: The reference geometry is held unchanged from the Builder's entity0: five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg, 0.16 x 0.14 m body. Its best controller so far (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, last_direction) scored 69.3241 in iterations 1, 4 and 6, so the geometry is reproducible. Iteration 7 tested base_speed 1.15 on this geometry and scored 61.765. Oval progress fell to 0.185 from 0.254, and line loss rose to 1.45 on oval, so the slower speed is rejected. The Builder's condition for confirming the geometry (about 69 with line loss at or below 1 per run) was not met, and the drop came from the controller. Line loss has stayed near 1 per run under every geometry, so the controller is the remaining lever. Steering oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.15), which leaves room for more derivative damping. I therefore restore base_speed 1.3 and make one controller change: kd 0.3 to 0.4, to damp the overshoot that precedes the abrupt line loss. Every other value stays at the reference. Sign check: positive x (left) carries a positive weight, so a line on the left steers left. Expected result: a score near 69.3 if kd has little effect, or a gain if it reduces line loss. This is a prediction, not a measurement, and I revert to kd 0.3 if the score falls.
